newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Treasurer to sell state notes competitively.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Treasurer to sell state notes competitively.

text.p: California will sell up to $3 billion of revenue anticipation notes (RANs) this year on a competitive rather than negotiated basis, state Treasurer Matt Fong announced on Thursday.
Fong's office said strong market demand for California bonds would make a competitive RANs sale "more advantageous" for the state than a negotiated sale.

"California is enjoying sustained economic growth, and the strong demand for our securities makes them a more valuable commodity on the market," Fong said in a statement. "In this environment, a competitive sale makes sense for taxpayers."
Each year the state treasurer sells RANs to meet the state's short-term cash needs. Typically, RANs are sold in August after the completion of the state's budget process.
Fong said this year's sale would take place after the budget is signed into law by the governor and after state finance officials meet with Wall Street rating agencies.
Fong said Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe would serve as note counsel for the sale and PRAG would serve as the state's financial advisor.
